factors.name: Size
factors.summary: Number of duplicate tasks (0.97), Size (0.97) and Token split (0.95) load very highly, so the factor captures how large the net is in nodes, labels and outgoing arcs. Density (-0.58) and Average connector degree (-0.48) load negatively, which fits larger nets being sparser, but both cross-load on Factor 3 and partly Factor 2.

factors.name: Connector degree / connectivity
factors.summary: Maximum connector degree (0.95) dominates, followed by Coefficient of network connectivity (0.66) and Average connector degree (0.46), so the factor reflects how many arcs meet at connectors and per node. Maximum connector degree has a communality at the bound of the fit (possible Heywood case), so the factor leans heavily on one measure.

factors.name: Connector homogeneity and density
factors.summary: Connector Heterogeneity loads strongly negatively (-0.93), while Density (0.61) and Average connector degree (0.58) load positively, so nets with a single connector type tend to be denser with busier connectors. Density and Average connector degree are cross-loading on Factor 1 (and Factor 2), so the factor is not a clean construct beyond the heterogeneity measure.

factors.name: Separability
factors.summary: Only Separability (0.63) is assigned, with moderate secondary loadings of Coefficient of network connectivity (0.48), Average connector degree (0.41) and Density (0.40) below the assignment rule. Its eigenvalue in the unrotated solution is below 1 and it explains about 11% of variance, so it is a weak factor.

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO of 0.75 exceeds 0.6, so the 288 nets are suitable for factor analysis after Sequentiality and Control flow complexity were removed by the MSA filter and Number of empty sequence flows was dropped as constant. The four varimax factors explain 85% of variance, separating a strong size factor from connector-degree, connector-homogeneity/density and a weak separability factor. However, only two eigenvalues exceed 1 and two factors were suggested, so Factors 3 and 4 may be over-extraction, and Connector Mismatch remains unassigned due to low communality (0.21).
caveats: Four factors were extracted although the eigenvalues and the suggestion support two, so Factors 3 and 4 may be unstable.
Maximum connector degree shows a possible Heywood case, which weakens trust in Factor 2.
Average connector degree and Density cross-load on several factors, blurring the distinction between Factors 1, 2 and 3.
Connector Mismatch is unassigned because of low communality, and Sequentiality and Control flow complexity were excluded by the MSA filter.
Factor 4 rests on a single measure and should be interpreted cautiously.
The factors reflect shared variance in this set of discovered nets and depend on the discovery algorithms, the rotation and the number of factors.
